Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
254 PM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Dry and warmer through the week.

2) Next chance of rain for late weekend into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Strong surface high pressure conditions to dominate the weather over 
much of the eastern half of the country through the end of the week and 
into the beginning of the weekend. As the high slowly shifts over the 
area into the middle to end of the week, temperatures will begin to 
moderate a bit more such that by Thursday and Friday, high temperatures 
will rise into the upper 50s to middle 60s. 

Given the clear and dry conditions under a weak pressure gradient, low 
temperatures each night through at least Thursday will be largely 
determined by the extent of radiational cooling. By Thursday night, a 
SW direction to the flow should allow subtle moisture advection which 
will limit the extent of the falling nighttime temperatures into the 
weekend.

.KEY MESSAGE 2...

By the second half of the weekend, a northern branch disturbance 
approaches the area from the northwest. At the same time, a mid level 
disturbance originating in the sub-tropics looks to develop a surface 
low pressure system that may move up the East Coast around the back 
side of the departing high. 

There remains ample differences between models in timing, strength, and 
the degree to which the northern and southern branch systems interact 
to have a more confident conclusion as to the impacts from this system 
at this time. For now, there is at least a decent chance for a
moisture-laden low pressure system to bring a period of moderate to
locally heavy rainfall to the area which brings with it the possibility
of several inches of rainfall over a 24 hour period somewhere in the
vicinity of the area sometime Sunday into Monday.

AI guidances are more consistent in bringing a more westward system 
which brings a steadier rainfall to the area. More traditional global 
models are less consistent in impacts to the area where the ECMWF
and the GFS bring a more eastward low pressure system which may
miss much the area in terms of more steady rainfall. 

That being said, subtle differences in timing and phasing of these two 
pieces of energy will ultimately determine what happens with this low 
pressure system, so confidence in impacts for the area from this system 
at this time remains low.

&&

.AVIATION /20Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
High pressure in control through the TAF period. VFR prevails. 

Wind speeds fall from 7-10 kt at most terminals to around or under
5 kt later tonight, with calm winds for some outlying terminals. 
The prevailing wind direction will be generally from the NW-W 
throughout the TAF period. Wind speeds will be generally 5 to 10
kt for late morning and afternoon Wednesday.      

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Wind directions could be off by 20-30 degrees from TAF at 
times this afternoon.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Wednesday through Sunday... 

Wednesday afternoon: VFR. Winds W-WNW 5-8 kt.

Thursday-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain in control of the weather through the week 
with sub-SCA conditions. Winds will mostly be from the NW-W at 
less than 15kt with seas on the ocean no higher than 2 to 3 ft.
